title: Websocket support on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
description:
This MR brings up support for HTTP upgraded protocol (aka extended CONNECT) and WebSocket dissection in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

It introduces following changes:
- Added request/response header tracking and lookup in HTTP/1 and HTTP/3 similarly to HTTP/2. Upgraded protocols need to have an ability to lookup request/response headers from HTTP transport.
- Replaced specific websocket header fields in HTTP/1 with the generic lookup method defined above
- Cleaned up version negotiation for upgraded protocol. According to https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-upgrade-tokens/http-upgrade-tokens.xhtml it is defined in a very specific way only for HTTP and TLS. Updated
- Removed CONNECT-UDP method from HTTP/3. It was never used in the wild and got replaced with connect-udp protocol in extended connect (RFC9298).
- Previously HTTP/3 tracked all bi-directional streams separately in server and client direction (since quic stream_info->from server is a part of lookup key). Added a check to merge directions.

Once this is approved I am planning to add dissection of HTTP Capsule protocol used in all HTTP versions for connect-ip, connect-udp and a number of upcoming standards.

This crashes on opening https://weberblog.net/the-ultimate-pcap/ (v20250325):  
```
      websocket_conv->subprotocol = http_info->get_header_value(pinfo, "sec-websocket-protocol", !http_info->from_server);

Exception has occurred: W32/0xC0000409
Unhandled exception at 0x00007FFE152FCC5F (ntdll.dll) in Wireshark.exe: Indirect call guard check detected invalid control transfer.
```

`pinfo->num: 8589`
Cannot see any websocket in the referenced "The Ultimate PCAP v20250325.pcapng". Packet 8589 seems to be generic non-web TCP data destined to port 1030. Any chance you are looking at some other PCAP?

Is protocol `websocket_tcp` enabled in your profile?  
Details below viewed in Wireshark 4.4.8.  
```
Frame 8589: 1518 bytes on wire (12144 bits), 1518 bytes captured (12144 bits) on interface \Device\NPF_{CD09206F-6D09-4F4E-B6BE-CA2FD3B8647D}, id 0
...
    Arrival Time: Nov  5, 2017 13:36:19.404273000 Central Standard Time
...
    [Protocols in frame: eth:ethertype:ip:tcp:websocket:data]
```
Thank you for finding this! I did replicate the issue and will submit an MR to fix this later today.

Fixed in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21035

FWIW, TCP heuristics based detection of websocket in this PCAP is a false positive, but of course it is still not a reason to crash.

Thanks for reporting the issue, @chuckcraft!

You have greatly increased memory consumption because this is now file scope but you are not looking it up if already exists in the non streaming chunk mode. So this file scoped header map gets created for every HTTP packet in every pass.

Indeed. `header_value_map` tracking is currently bogus. Working on a fix...
Thanks for pointing this out.

+#define HTTP2_HEADER_PROTOCOL ":protocol"
 #define HTTP2_HEADER_UNKNOWN "<unknown>"
